URL REFERENCE PROTOCOL
The application keeps an exact mapping from each observed source ID (such as <url>U1</url>) to its original URL, including path, query parameters and signature. <url>U1</url> is an opaque, session-local address, not a website's article/video ID. The domain field is only a source identity hint, not a replacement address. To read a source already returned by a tool, copy its ID unchanged into web_extract's urls array. The application resolves it before making the real request. Do not reconstruct a URL from its domain, title or ID; do not append IDs to https://, paths, watch URLs, query parameters or search queries. A literal URL is allowed when supplied explicitly by the user or already visible in evidence.
Only actual tool observations in this session introduce usable IDs. These instructional examples do not register any IDs. Never guess the next ID, use a future result, or use one parallel call's result before it has returned in a subsequent turn. Parent and child sessions have separate ID scopes; retain IDs unchanged across summaries within one session. If an ID is unknown, use an already visible source or search for the missing information.
For web_search, use natural-language factual queries, not source IDs. For web_extract, use a JSON array value in the XML urls parameter, not a quoted JSON string. Keep source references attached to their claims in summaries and answers; never invent a full URL for a citation. An ID identifies evidence, not proof: inspect its title, domain and content, respect failed extraction, and do not treat an error/login/empty page or matching search title as factual confirmation.
Representation rule: in prose, reasoning, citations and summaries, write <url>U1</url> without padding spaces. In tool arguments, pass only the inner ID: urls=["U1"]. Do not include XML tags in argument values. The application resolves this ID to the exact original URL; you never need to reconstruct the path. A visible XML source or evidence reference satisfies source-URL citation requirements; do not invent a literal address to satisfy older URL wording.

modes.hybrid: MODE hybrid: a source's first observation can include both its literal URL and source_ref. Later observations may show only the ID. Prefer the source_ref for extraction whenever available; its exact destination remains the same. When source_ref is <url>U5</url>, pass "U5" in the urls array.
modes.ref: MODE ref: source url fields contain U references and a separate domain. The complete address is intentionally hidden from the prompt and retained by the application. Pass the inner U ID (without XML tags) to web_extract; no URL reconstruction is necessary.
modes.evidence: MODE evidence: U references identify source URLs; <url>Dn@vM</url> identifies an immutable page-content snapshot; <url>Dn@vM#Ek</url> identifies a span in that snapshot. The initial page observation may show only its first two spans. If truncated is true or a needed claim is absent, read the relevant remaining spans with web_extract before concluding it is absent or citing it. available_spans is the maximum valid span number; do not invent documents or versions. Re-reading the document ID without #E returns only its first two spans. Use separate calls for stored D references and live U/URL targets. In tool arguments use bare snapshot/span IDs, for example urls=["D6@v1#E3"]; in prose cite <url>D6@v1#E3</url>.

ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE 1 — read an observed source (IDs below are not live registrations).
Tool observation: {"data":{"web":[{"url":"<url>U1</url>","domain":"archive.example.org","title":"Annual report","description":"Report for the requested year"}]}}
Assistant tool call:
<tool_call>
<function=web_extract>
<parameter=urls>["U1"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
The program reads the exact original report URL. Do not replace this action with https://archive.example.org/ or https://archive.example.org/report?id=U1.

ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE 2 — multiple observed sources and an unavailable reference.
Tool observation: two search results expose <url>U2</url> and <url>U3</url>.
Assistant tool call:
<tool_call>
<function=web_extract>
<parameter=urls>["U2", "U3"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
If a fourth source is needed but has not been returned, search by the missing factual clue instead of guessing <url>U4</url>:
<tool_call>
<function=web_search>
<parameter=query>annual report publication date official archive</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
Wait for its actual observation before using any newly returned ID.

evidence:
ILLUSTRATIVE EXAMPLE 3 — retrieve unseen evidence within an observed snapshot.
Tool observation: {"url":"<url>U6</url>","document_ref":"<url>D6@v1</url>","content":"<url>D6@v1#E1</url> Introduction ... <url>D6@v1#E2</url> Contents ...","available_spans":4,"truncated":true}
The initial spans do not contain the requested figures. Read remaining spans:
<tool_call>
<function=web_extract>
<parameter=urls>["D6@v1#E3", "D6@v1#E4"]</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
Tool observation: {"results":[{"document_ref":"<url>D6@v1</url>","content":"<url>D6@v1#E3</url> The reported count is 12.","cached":true},{"document_ref":"<url>D6@v1</url>","content":"<url>D6@v1#E4</url> Notes on measurement.","cached":true}]}
Assistant answer: The report gives a count of 12 <url>D6@v1#E3</url>.
Do not cite an unread span or ask for <url>D6@v2</url> unless that version was actually observed.

tool_descriptions.web_search: Search using factual words, not source IDs. Returned <url>U1</url> references identify exact source URLs held by the application. Use only references from actual tool observations; examples do not register sources.
tool_descriptions.web_extract: URL reference adapter: if an observation shows <url>U1</url>, pass urls=["U1"]. For several sources pass urls=["U1", "U2"]. The array values are bare IDs, without XML tags. The program restores the exact original paths and query parameters. Never append an ID to a domain or fabricate a URL from its title. Literal HTTP(S) URLs remain accepted when actually provided. In prose and citations retain <url>U1</url>.
tool_descriptions.vision_analyze: When a visible image source is identified as <url>U1</url>, pass image_url="U1", without XML tags. The program restores its exact URL. Use only image sources actually observed; otherwise retain the supported literal URL or data-URI format.

evidence.web_extract: For an observed snapshot <url>D6@v1</url> with available_spans=4, read later spans using urls=["D6@v1#E3", "D6@v1#E4"]. Cite read evidence as <url>D6@v1#E3</url>. Do not invent a version or exceed available_spans. Use separate calls for stored snapshot IDs and live U IDs or URLs.
